after: 2026-09-26|Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off

2026-05-14|The rest of the country.headline: The rest of the country
2026-05-14|The rest of the country.text: The revision was ordered in 16 states and 3 union territories, covering the whole country except Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, whose dates would be announced later. Eight separate schedules were set. After the draft, notices would go to those who could not be linked to the last intensive revision (the no-mapping list) and to those whose link showed a discrepancy. Lists of those sent notices were to be published.

2026-09-26|Documents at the door, and a.id: 2026-09-26|Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off
2026-09-26|Documents at the door, and a.headline: Documents at the door, and a drive for those left off
2026-09-26|Documents at the door, and a.text: For people sent notices as unmapped or for logical discrepancies, BLOs would collect documents at home and upload them for the registration officer, so these people need not come to the office. A hearing would be held only in exceptional cases, as the registration officer decides, preferably online, and a family member authorised by the elector could attend. The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply. Claims were extended in Delhi to 30 October and in Maharashtra to 12 October 2026. Where the revision was complete, in 20 states and union territories, anyone left out during it or after, and any young or first-time voter, could ask the registration officer to be added under continuous updation, and the Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers were to launch a special drive at once to enrol them.

court-37.headline: SIR-Deleted Voters Move Supreme Court For Expeditious Disposal Of Appeals Before Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
court-37.text: Five electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication applied to the Supreme Court for their appeals to be decided before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections, LiveLaw reported. They also asked for a Special Investigation Team to examine how the revision's decisions were made. The application cites the Commission's affidavits as showing 1.7 lakh appeals pending from Kolkata and Howrah.
court-37.quote: the applicants claim that their names were deleted without any notice to them.
court-37.response: None was reported. The applicants say the Chief Electoral Officer has not published the criteria for logical discrepancies.

court-54.headline: Delhi SIR : Why Deleted Voters Asked To File Form 6 When They Were On 2026 Rolls? Supreme Court Asks ECI
court-54.text: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana asked the Election Commission on 28 October why electors left off Delhi's draft for not returning enumeration forms are asked to apply on Form 6, which is meant for first-time voters, when they were on the roll of 2026, LiveLaw reported. Justice Bagchi said the Commission's four categories leave no place for electors who were never served a form, such as someone away from Delhi for a month, and that if the roll of 2026 is the base an elector who has shifted should be allowed Form 8. The bench suggested a residual category for those temporarily away, asked the Commission to reach out to electors given Delhi's floating population, and, as Bar and Bench reported, said the excluded names must be easily accessible in simple Hindi and local languages. Bar and Bench also reported Justice Bagchi saying the Court had not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful, and had allowed it in West Bengal only as an interim arrangement. Counsel for the petitioners, Prashant Bhushan, said 43 of the 47 lakh left off are shown as permanently shifted or absent. The Indian Express reported that the bench said electors left off the draft who had only been away for a time should be allowed to submit the enumeration form, and those who had moved to another address in Delhi should be allowed Form 8. The Chief Justice suggested a statement or circular saying that Form 6 is to be filled only by those registering as voters in Delhi for the first time, LiveLaw and The Indian Express reported, and The Indian Express reported him adding that it was not for those on the roll of 2026 who could not fill the enumeration form because they had moved or were away. Hindustan Times reported the Court asking for a public notice saying that Form 6 is for first-time enrolment and that those who had moved could use Form 8 or the enumeration form. The Chief Justice also told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election is due in Delhi, to keep inviting Form 6 and Form 8 and verify the documents attached, and to issue a public notice in newspapers and online that the process is continuing, The Indian Express reported. The Times of India reported the bench's suggestion that the Commission publish the list of electors left off with the reason against each name, ask them to contact the nearest booth level officer and fill Form 8, give them enumeration forms and tell them they may fill either Form 6 or Form 8. The bench listed the matter after two weeks. The Indian Express reported that the bench said it was not issuing an order to extend the deadline of 30 October and expected the Commission to act on its own, and The Times of India reported that the bench spoke without passing any order. No written order was reported. Anjali Bhardwaj, one of the two petitioners, wrote on X on 30 October that the Court had said electors on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors should be allowed to fill the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which she wrote requires them to make a false declaration that they are first-time voters. She wrote that 32 lakh of the 47 lakh on that list in Delhi were marked permanently shifted and 12 lakh untraceable or absent.
court-54.quote: In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category. We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,
court-54.response: Senior Advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the Commission, said the authorities would examine the concerns, take remedial steps and consider extending the deadline, LiveLaw reported. He said the roll of 2026 before the revision is the base. Bar and Bench reported that the Commission would consider accepting late enumeration forms and would extend the deadline of 30 October if needed. The Indian Express reported Naidu telling the bench that the Commission would report its steps in two weeks and that the time would be extended in the meanwhile. The Times of India reported him saying that the Commission had held more than one lakh camps in Delhi, that not a single person had come to fill Form 8, and that no one had been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore a name.

form7-102.headline: Deletion of father’s name from voter list poses hurdle to infant’s birth certificate
form7-102.text: A two and a half month old infant in Cooch Behar district has been denied a birth certificate as a result of the deletion of her father's name from the roll during the revision, The Hindu reported on 24 November. The girl was born on 9 September at the sub-divisional hospital in Dinhata. The paper reports that when her parents approached the hospital and the panchayat office for the certificate, they were asked to arrange residential verification from the panchayat pradhan or the MLA, that the office of the MLA for Dinhata, Ajoy Roy, refused the father's request for the verification, and that the father was told the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the roll. The father told the paper that an official from the MLA's office said he was a Bangladeshi national and would first have to register through the National Register of Citizens. He said he has lived in India since his birth, that his house was built by his grandfather, and that he had shown all his documents and was still refused. He said the block development officer of Sahebganj refused a similar request on the same grounds. The paper reports that the names of three of his sisters were also deleted, that the Commission had called them for a hearing citing a logical discrepancy that six other persons had given the name of his father, and that his parents, his wife and an elder sister are on the roll. He has appealed to a tribunal to have his name included. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights said in a statement that birth registration is a statutory obligation, that every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, and that a child's right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents, and demanded that the government provide the certificate at once. The Wire carried the same account on 25 November. On 23 November the Supreme Court issued notice on an application asking it to direct the state to withdraw notifications that restrict the welfare benefits of electors deleted in the revision (court-96).
form7-102.quote: An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore, I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth.
form7-102.response: The report carries no statement from the MLA, his office, the panchayat, the block development officer, the hospital or the Chief Electoral Officer. The paper states the refusal by the MLA's office in its own words. The official's remark on nationality and the refusal by the block development officer are the father's account.

form7-54.headline: Uttarakhand ERO refused BJP worker’s bulk Form 7 objections. After ECI complaint, 5,359 were accepted
form7-54.text: Newslaundry found 4,390 names on Kichha's draft roll that are missing from the final roll published on 3 October. About 670 of them had Form 7 objections filed against them in August, 509 by a single BJP booth level agent, and the other 3,720 had no objection against them and were deleted on the ground of logical discrepancies. Of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted in Kichha, 5,359 were that agent's, and he filed more Form 7 objections than anyone else in Uttarakhand. He told Newslaundry that the Electoral Registration Officer at first refused his bulk objections and took them after he complained to the Election Commission by email, and Newslaundry could not verify what the email said. Form 10 data from the Chief Electoral Officer's office show 504 of his accepted objections with an acceptance date of 14 August, a day after claims and objections closed. Newslaundry reported that every name in his objections was Muslim. He said the party had received information that about 6,000 electors enrolled in Kichha were also enrolled in five nearby constituencies of Uttar Pradesh.
form7-54.quote: Of the 4,390 names missing from Kichha’s final electoral roll, 3,720 had no objections filed against them. The ERO deleted these voters on the basis of logical discrepancies, a mismatch in voter data that the ECI believes requires additional verification before the electoral roll is finalised.
form7-54.response: The Kichha Electoral Registration Officer, Gaurav Pandey, neither confirmed nor denied the agent's account, would not say whether the Commission had directed him, and said the deletions followed the Commission's rules. Newslaundry said the Commission acknowledged its questions and did not answer them, and that it had asked the Chief Electoral Officer why objections were accepted after the deadline. The Congress MLA for Kichha, Tilak Raj Behar, said the objections rested on false information. The report does not say how it established the electors' religion.

form7-56.headline: Over 61,000 Form-7 applications filed by election officials in Karnataka, none cites reason
form7-56.text: At least 61,059 Form 7 applications seeking deletions from Karnataka's rolls were filed by Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers themselves, and none gives a reason for the deletion, which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require, The Hindu reported. Officers listed as the objectors said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies could not be reached at hearings and were marked ineligible. Only 192 such applications were filed between 24 August and 23 September, and more than 60,800 between 24 September and 22 October, including 10,105 on 22 October, the last day for disposal. The paper's chart puts more than 53,000 of the officers' applications in the week from 16 to 22 October, with the most on one day, 11,760, on 19 October. In every case the paper checked on the Commission's portal the elector had already been deleted, including electors against whom the application came after 23 September. In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district officers filed 10,374 of 17,491 applications, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more than voters or third parties did.
form7-56.quote: Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), listed as the objectors in these applications, said the system “auto-generated” the forms with their digital signatures when voters could not be reached during hearings on notices issued for no mapping or logical discrepancies, and the voters were therefore marked as “ineligible”.
form7-56.response: The officers said they had been told to file Form 7 for electors who had shifted, had a duplicate entry, were underage, had died or were not citizens. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. Rule 17 of the 1960 Rules says a claim or objection not lodged within the period or in the prescribed form and manner shall be rejected by the registration officer. The paper also found 13,808 fewer Form 7 applications for 24 September to 22 October in the Commission's Form 10 records than the Chief Electoral Officer's statements give.

https://diagramchasing.fun/2026/karnatak.headline: No eligible citizen is left out (?)
https://diagramchasing.fun/2026/karnatak.text: Aman Bhargava of Diagram Chasing tests the line printed on every page of the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer's summary booklet for the final roll, that no eligible citizen is left out and no ineligible person is included, against the rolls themselves. He read all 60,923 booth files of the final roll of 27 October by machine and joined them by EPIC number to digitised copies of the 2002 roll, the January 2025 roll, the list of names left off the draft and the notice lists, which the groups Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka made. He reports that of 1,05,48,148 electors left off the draft whom he found on the January 2025 roll, about 14,900 came back on the final roll in the same constituency with the same name, relative and age, and that 206 of 8.9 lakh aged 75 and over came back. He counts 3,115 electors told they were not on the 2002 roll although the Chief Electoral Officer's own copy of it carries them under the same EPIC number, 4,954 deleted after a notice that flagged children born less than nine months apart, a rule that catches twins, 8,992 people on the roll more than once in their own booth, 461 EPIC numbers on the roll in two constituencies and 234 new voters in Dasarahalli given an EPIC number held earlier by someone left off the draft. He finds the share of electors sent a notice ranging from 0.03 per cent in Mayakonda to 59 per cent in C.V. Raman Nagar, and nine constituencies where no notice ended in a finding of ineligibility. He says his counts are minimums, that the rolls by themselves cannot establish identity, and that the work rests on optical character recognition of files the Commission publishes as PDFs.

https://internetfreedom.in/analysis-and-.headline: Analysis and Explainer on the Software of the SIR That Runs Without Transparency
https://internetfreedom.in/analysis-and-.text: It describes the systems behind the revision (ECINET, the BLO app, ERONET run by TCS since 2023, the mapping and 'logical discrepancy' rules, machine transliteration and duplicate-detection tools) and finds that none has a published specification, threshold or audit. Citing The Reporters' Collective, it gives 1.31 crore electors flagged in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh by the discrepancy rules.

https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/28/indi.headline: India: Mass Voter Roll Exclusions Deeply Flawed
https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/28/indi.text: Human Rights Watch says it has interviewed 70 people in Delhi, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Karnataka since August, among them 40 whose families were affected by the revision, former election commissioners, lawyers, activists and a serving electoral official. It finds that people were excluded for mismatched names, spelling errors, having six or more siblings or siblings born less than nine months apart, and that the software flagged Adivasi and Muslim names disproportionately, in part because their spellings vary. It finds that the authorities used data from the revision to deny passport renewals, food rations, a West Bengal cash transfer for women, scholarships and residence certificates, including to people whose appeals were still pending. It describes the bulk use of Form 7 against Muslim voters as the media reported it, transgender people excluded because their documents carry different names, and security forces beating and arresting protesters in October 2026. Its Asia director, Elaine Pearson, calls for the revision to be scrapped and for everyone wrongly excluded to regain the vote promptly.

process-11.headline: How ECI’s dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
process-11.text: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
process-11.response: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

process-12.headline: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
process-12.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
process-12.response: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

process-13.headline: The many categories of SIR’s logical discrepancy list keep voters on toes
process-13.text: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

process-16.headline: 8 emails in 7 days, but valid Goa voters still left out: EC’s flawed system
process-16.text: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
process-16.response: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

rti-08.headline: TMC's Saket Gokhale says EC 'withholding' details of SIR software, cites RTI response
rti-08.text: Technical documents on the 'logical discrepancy' module in ERONET used for the West Bengal SIR, its logic and parameters, procurement and testing records, file notings, instructions to EROs, and the number of electors flagged under each sub-category. Deccan Herald (PTI) reported that the Commission held the software questions exempt under Section 8(1)(d), said no module or separate procurement had been made for the West Bengal SIR, and directed the question on flagged electors to the EROs.
rti-08.quote: No separate procurement and development has been made for SIR in West Bengal.

rti-09.headline: ECI has no record of what constitutes 'logical discrepancy' in SIR, RTI reply shows
rti-09.text: The definition of 'logical discrepancy' in any official document and the number of notices issued to electors in the 10 States and UTs where the SIR was complete. The News Minute reported that the Commission said the information was not available with it and might be with the CEOs of the States and UTs.
rti-09.quote: The information sought by you is not available in the Commission. It may be available with the Office of the CEO of States/UTs

soft-07.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
soft-07.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
soft-07.quote: The discrepancies were of five kinds, as per ECI’s new algorithm: Differences in spelling between the names in the 2002 in Bengali script and in the 2025 draft voter rolls in English More than six voters had linked themselves to a single ancestor from the 2003 list; The age gap between a voter and their parent fell outside the 15-to-45-year range; A cited grandparent was less than 40 years older than the voter; The gender of the voter did not align with the name provided.
soft-07.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

soft-08.headline: How ECI Tailored the Voter Registration in West Bengal “As it Deemed Fit”
soft-08.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
soft-08.quote: “These options keep changing every other day,” the ERO told me. “Till this morning, for logical discrepancies with name mismatch, ERONET was allowing me to verify the elector by myself. Now, when I open ERONET, that button has disappeared. Now, these have to be approved by the DEO.”
soft-08.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

soft-12.headline: Verified: ECI’s top West Bengal officer sent orders to state officials for SIR on WhatsApp
soft-12.text: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
soft-12.quote: On December 29, after the enumeration phase was complete, the CEO West Bengal’s office admitted on record to state officials that the software finding ‘logical discrepancies’ was malfunctioning. This was because the base data, the 2002 voter list, had not been digitised accurately, the CEO admitted.
soft-12.response: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

soft-13.headline: Order of 19.01.2026, W.P.(C) 1089/2025
soft-13.text: The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
soft-13.quote: The documents brought on record by the parties indicate that, within the category of logical discrepancies include, inter alia, a mismatch of the father’s name, a mismatch of parents’ ages, a difference in parents’ ages of more than 50 years, a difference in grandparents’ ages of less than 40 years, and those having more than six progeny.

soft-15.headline: Press note No.EL.63/2026/50: CEO Meghalaya Reviews Notice and Hearing Phase of SIR 2026
soft-15.text: Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.
soft-15.quote: The discrepancies identified through ECINET are: mismatch between the elector's name and the name available in the SIR 2005 records; mismatch between the elector's parent's name and the corresponding name recorded in SIR 2005; age difference between the elector and parent being less than 15 years or more than 50 years; age gap of less than nine months between siblings linked to the same parent; more than six children being linked to the same parent; and age difference of less than 40 years between an elector and grandparent.

soft-40.headline: Pending SIR notice lists published for only 39 assembly constituencies out of 288 so far
soft-40.text: Lists of electors whose notices were still pending had been published for 39 of Maharashtra's 288 Assembly constituencies, in 14 districts, on the election authorities' websites by Saturday 24 October, The Times of India reported. Officials said the lists hold only unresolved cases and do not cover all 1.22 crore notices generated in the revision. In Pune district only the Shivajinagar list was up, with one elector on it, and in Mumbai the lists for Malabar Hill, Byculla, Dharavi, Dahisar and Vandre West. A circular of 23 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office told electoral registration officers to download the data from the Commission's ECINET platform, compile one PDF for each constituency, publish it on the district election officer's website by 26 October and share part-wise lists with parties' booth level agents. Officials said documents some electors had given booth level officers during enumeration were not uploaded because the system did not support it then. Notices are to be disposed of by 10 November and the final roll is due on 16 November.
soft-40.quote: The lists cover voters whose names could not be matched with previous electoral rolls, categorised as ‘No Mapping’, and those whose records showed logical discrepancies despite successful mapping. A name appearing on the list does not mean the voter has been finally deleted from the electoral roll,
soft-40.response: An electoral official said a name on the list does not mean the elector has been finally deleted from the roll, and the report says the Chief Electoral Officer's office will review whether district election authorities have complied with the circular.

soft-45.headline: Did 27 Lakhs Lose the Right to Vote Because the EC Software Switched Bengal Voters Already Decided by EROs Over to Judges Overnight?
soft-45.text: A screen recording of the Commission's officer portal seen by The Wire shows how the logical discrepancy check flagged a woman in Deganga, North 24 Parganas, born in 1977, The Wire reported. She had named her father and the portal had found him in the 2002 roll. Under the heading 'Logical Discrepancies' the portal gave a single reason, that six other electors had also named the same man as their father, and the only option on the screen was to schedule a hearing. A leader of a booth level officers' association in West Bengal told The Wire that the BLO app changed about 16 times during the revision and that the logical discrepancy system 'was done from Delhi'. The Wire reported that booth level officers were told to verify the flagged electors in person and did so, and the leader said their reports were submitted through the software and no action was taken on them. He said the then Chief Electoral Officer, Manoj Kumar Agarwal, had told the association that his office was forwarding its letters to Delhi and that 'Whatever is being done is being done from Delhi'.
soft-45.quote: You have been linked as son/daughter with someone who is also claimed by six others as father, giving suspicion of a likely incorrect match.
soft-45.response: The Wire says it asked Agarwal to confirm the remark the association leader attributes to him and that it will update the report when he replies. No reply is reported.

soft-53.headline: Election Commission completes Form 6 U-turn, drops SIR para a Commissioner called ‘illegal’
soft-53.text: The Election Commission has taken the SIR declaration out of the online Form 6 on its ECINet portal in the states where the revision is still running, and the declaration is now on the portal as a separate form, The Indian Express reported on 4 November. The declaration sat between Sections J and K of the online form and asked an applicant to say whether their own name, or a parent's or grandparent's, was on the roll of the last intensive revision, and an applicant could not go on without answering it. The paper reports that the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) records a decision of its ER Division of 21 October that the online application would be in two parts, Form 6 and the SIR declaration, as the paper forms are, and that this is what the portal now shows. After the Commission's note of 26 September the declaration had been taken off the online form only in the states where the revision had ended. The paper also reports that four changes to ECINet that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, S. Chockalingam, sought in a letter of 24 September have been made. Personal hearings for electors sent notices over mapping or logical discrepancies are now held only in exceptional cases, with booth level officers collecting documents at home. Electors may give documents outside the listed categories. Registration officers can decide logical-discrepancy cases themselves without sending them to the District Election Officer. The upload of an extract from the previous SIR roll is no longer mandatory. The paper reports that applicants filing Form 6 in the special summary revision ordered for 17 states and union territories will not have to fill the SIR declaration. The paper reports that a committee to check whether ECINet complies with the applicable Acts and Rules was constituted by a circular of 14 October. It is headed by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner and includes a second Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, a Deputy Election Commissioner, a director, four Chief Electoral Officers and two independent experts, from IIT Bombay and IISc Bengaluru. On Goa, the paper reports that the Chief Electoral Officer has been directed to see that the 97 electors left off the final roll are included. It reports that the affidavit says 88 of them have filled in Form 6 and had their applications accepted, that six are out of the country and that three hold Portuguese passports. On West Bengal, the paper reports that the affidavit does not give the number of appeals filed against the inclusion of electors, that the appeals have not been withdrawn, and that the affidavit says the electors concerned are on the rolls and voted in the recent Assembly elections.
soft-53.quote: What this means is that the declaration inserted between Sections J and K of the online enrolment application for new voters is no longer part of Form 6.
soft-53.response: The Commission's counter affidavit, as the paper quotes it, maintains that Form 6 was never amended: "There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the Commission vide the SIR Orders." It says the declaration was placed inside the online Form 6 so that an applicant would need a single OTP and a single e-signature.

soft-54.headline: Delhi SIR: Aadhaar alone not enough, BLOs asked to seek ‘citizenship proof’ from voters
soft-54.text: Booth level officers in several Delhi constituencies told The Hindu that registration officers were sending them back to electors who had answered a notice for no mapping with only an Aadhaar card, to collect further documents as proof of citizenship, after the officers had filed field verification reports and undertakings that the electors were eligible and had lived at their addresses for years. One officer said his registration officer called him on 2 November, after he had finished verifying all his cases, and asked him to gather proof of citizenship. Another said the instructions on documents had changed repeatedly. Officers said they had been told at a meeting on 1 October that their undertakings could be accepted where electors had none of the prescribed documents. The Hindu says it saw electors who gave only Aadhaar flagged on the system used by registration officers and their assistants, and an officer said an elector who had given a passport was also asked for documents again. Of nearly 97 lakh electors on Delhi's draft, 33.1 lakh were sent notices, 13.9 lakh for no mapping and the rest for logical discrepancies, and data the Chief Electoral Officer's office shared the week before showed more than 94% of the 33.1 lakh marked for the final roll. The time to decide notices runs to 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December.
soft-54.quote: I was asked to gather citizenship proof. The voters have been living there for many years, and there are many in my area who never went to school
soft-54.response: Officials denied that any such instruction had been issued and said no identification or record of 'illegal immigrants' on the roll is being kept. A senior official said that Aadhaar alone was not sufficient, that a registration officer could still mark an elector eligible on a satisfactory field report, and that neither mapping nor logical discrepancies affect an elector's eligibility. Officials said a registration officer not satisfied with the documents could mark an elector ineligible through a speaking order recording the reasons. A registration officer said officials were first told during enumeration to identify foreign nationals on the rolls, that the direction was changed soon after, and that no such list is being prepared.

soft-67.headline: ECI’s Bengal SIR Dashboard Used Hard-Coded Numbers Instead of Live Data, Code Analysis Finds
soft-67.text: Some of West Bengal's figures on ECINet, the Election Commission's online system for managing the electoral rolls, are written into the code of its pages, so that they stay the same whatever the Commission's database holds, according to an analysis The Wire reported on 24 November. The Wire says it began looking into the code after a tip-off, asked three senior computer scientists and a cybersecurity expert, none of whom wishes to be named, to examine the findings, and read the code as it stood on 18 November, which the server records as last changed on 16 October. By The Wire's account, the dashboard of electors flagged for logical discrepancies shows the database's figure for every state except West Bengal, where the code shows 94,49,132, which The Wire says is the official count of the state's electors flagged in the verification. On a second dashboard the code sets West Bengal's notices at 1,51,92,735 and works out the number of hearings from that figure, and The Wire says the only other figure the code replaces on that dashboard is Tamil Nadu's count of cases found not OK. The Wire reports that the rules used to flag electors are written into the West Bengal dashboard. They are a parent linked to six or more children on the roll, a father's name that does not match, a parent and child less than 15 or more than 50 years apart in age, and a grandparent and grandchild less than 40 years apart. The analysis also found a backup screen for turnout that shows 2,84,19,840 votes from 3,60,77,304 electors, 78.77%, marked as last updated on 11 April 2026, which The Wire matches to the turnout at 3 pm on 23 April, the first day of polling. The Wire says it sent its questions to the Commission on 21 November and that on 23 November the portal was redeployed and visitors to its code files were sent to a login page.
soft-67.quote: When West Bengal is chosen, the code shows 94,49,132, whatever the database says.
soft-67.response: The Wire says the Commission had not answered its questions when the report was published, and that the Commission has not said whether the restriction on the code was connected to them. The Wire says the analysis rests only on the files the portal sends to browsers, that it cannot show what the Commission's servers hold or why the fixed figures are there, and that it found no field for religion, caste or community and no feature that deletes electors automatically at this stage.

up-49.headline: Gems of UP SSR: 1.1 lakh voters whose parent is younger to them or of same age
up-49.text: Alt News counted 1,10,875 electors on Uttar Pradesh's draft roll of the summary revision, published on 17 November, whose entry names a father or a mother who is listed in the same polling station and the same house with the same age as the elector or a younger one, in a report by Ankit Jain published on 23 November. Alt News says it took every elector whose entry names a father or a mother and looked in the same polling station for an elector of that name living in the same house. In 35,523 of the cases the parent and the child are listed with the same age, and in the other 75,352 the parent is younger, in 6,860 of them by 20 years or more. Alt News says the cases are spread across all 75 districts and all 403 Assembly constituencies, that Kushinagar district has the most, 3,646, and that Fazilnagar has the most of any constituency, 711. It recalls that in the intensive revision a parent less than 15 years older than the elector was one of what the Commission called logical discrepancies, which Alt News says its software looked for, that about 2.22 crore electors in Uttar Pradesh were sent notices for such discrepancies, and that the Commission says hearings were completed on all of them. Alt News says all 1,10,875 are on the draft, which it puts at 13.58 crore electors, and that claims and objections can be filed till 16 December, with the final roll due on 4 January 2027.
up-49.quote: We found 1,10,875 such cases spread across all 75 districts and 403 constituencies.
up-49.response: The report carries no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission, and none was found. Every count is Alt News's own, from the draft roll. The report matches a parent to an elector by name within one house and polling station, and it does not say how it treated two electors of the same name in one house.
